module_title: Gupta Empire and Harsha - Art, Science, Literature, and Administration
introduction: This level focuses on the elements that made the Gupta period the 'Golden Age'. It covers unprecedented advancements in science, mathematics, astronomy, and literature, along with Harsha's administrative reforms and religious assemblies.

core_concepts.title: Development in Science and Mathematics
core_concepts.description: Scholars like Aryabhata (concept of zero, rotation of the earth) and Varahamihira (astronomy) took science to new heights during the Gupta era.

core_concepts.title: Golden Age of Literature
core_concepts.description: Sanskrit literature flourished with the works of Kalidasa (Abhijnanashakuntalam, Meghaduta), Vishakhadatta (Mudrarakshasa), and Shudraka (Mricchakatika).

core_concepts.title: Origins of Temple Architecture
core_concepts.description: The construction of permanent temples using bricks and stones began during the Gupta period, a prime example being the Dashavatara Temple at Deogarh (Panchayatana style).

core_concepts.title: Harsha's Administration
core_concepts.description: Harsha's administration was more feudal compared to the centralized system of the Mauryas/Guptas. His tax system was primarily divided into three types: Bhaga, Hiranya, and Bali.

core_concepts.title: Harsha's Religious Assemblies
core_concepts.description: Harshavardhana organized a grand assembly at Kannauj to promote Mahayana Buddhism, and the 'Maha Moksha Parishad' every five years at Prayag.

important_entities.name: Aryabhata
important_entities.significance: Authored Surya Siddhanta and Aryabhatiya; calculated the value of Pi (π).

important_entities.name: Kalidasa
important_entities.significance: The most prominent among the 'Navaratnas' of Chandragupta II.

important_entities.name: Banabhatta
important_entities.significance: Authored the famous texts 'Harshacharita' (biography of Harsha) and 'Kadambari'.

important_entities.name: Nalanda University
important_entities.significance: Founded by Kumaragupta I, but reached its peak and received massive patronage during Harsha's reign.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Because Hiuen Tsang studied there and Harsha heavily patronized it, students often assume Harsha built it. In reality, it was founded by the Gupta ruler 'Kumaragupta I'.
While powerful in the North, Harsha was not undefeated. His southern expansion was halted when he was defeated by the Chalukya king 'Pulakeshin II' on the banks of the Narmada River.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: The three plays written by Harsha: P - Priyadarshika, N - Nagananda, R - Ratnavali.
Connect Kumaragupta (Kumar) with Nalanda (Nala) to remember the founder.

exam_strategy_tips: Practice matching questions involving ancient books and their authors (e.g., Mudrarakshasa-Vishakhadatta, Harshacharita-Banabhatta).
Memorize the locations of prominent Gupta temples (like Bhitargaon, Deogarh) on the map.
